MENA service sector, largely uninfrastructured

The problem

MENA's service providers are running blind.

Not a guess — it is what the market looks like across Egypt and the Gulf.

90% run on WhatsApp and Excel

They lose more than 40% of potential bookings with no availability tracking, and carry no-show rates above 25% with no automated reminders.

Discovered on social, booked offline

80% of consumers find services on social media and then book in a chat. There is no structured way to appear where people actually search and book.

Every platform is a silo

Even when listed, a provider cannot control pricing, availability or presence across channels. Update one, update the rest by hand.

The product

Three steps. Instant distribution.

A provider signs up, adds services and availability, and appears on every connected platform at once.

One provider dashboard

Services, staff, branches, calendar, CRM, payments, visibility and analytics — the business managed in one place.

Many consumer storefronts

shaaml.online, OurBride and our-bazaar.com today, with beauty and lifestyle platforms next. One provider record, every shopfront.

Verticals that widen

Wedding, beauty, photography and events are live. Home services and healthcare are year two; automotive and food year three.

How it works

Seven steps, and step one is free.

The free step is the acquisition strategy. A provider gets real market research for their own city before paying anything, and the gap between knowing and acting is what the other six steps sell.

  1. 01

    Market research

    Real demand in the provider's city: what sells, at what price, against whom. Free, and included in the base plan — the hook.

  2. 02

    One hero offer

    A single focused service instead of a menu. Complexity removed, decisions made faster.

  3. 03

    Conversion asset

    A WhatsApp-ready booking page with a clear price, the benefit and one call to action.

  4. 04

    Traffic injection

    Local Facebook and Instagram campaigns, radius and interest targeted, on a controlled budget.

  5. 05

    Lead qualification

    WhatsApp question flows filter for budget, date and location, so only serious leads reach the provider.

  6. 06

    Closing and follow-up

    Arabic reply scripts, objection handling for the real ones — «غالي», «هفكر» — and automated sequences.

  7. 07

    Optimisation loop

    Weekly: scale what worked, kill what did not, drive cost per lead down. This is the part that compounds.

Why this wins

They manage or they distribute. We do both.

This is the whole argument, and it is a structural one rather than a feature comparison.

Fresha, Mindbody and Booksy help a provider manage

Excellent tools for running the business. They do not put the provider in front of new customers.

Marketplace apps help a provider get found

Demand, but no control — the provider is a listing inside somebody else's storefront, with no say over pricing or presence.

Nobody does both

Shaaml is the only platform where a provider manages the business and is distributed to multiple consumer storefronts from the same record.

Built before the money

Providers onboarded, bookings processed and three platforms live pre-funding. The capital buys growth, not construction.

Already built

Most of this already exists.

The Growth Engine is not a new platform. It is a module on foundations that are already in production — which is why the build risk sits closer to zero than a pre-revenue company usually gets.

Guider platform

33 entities and 300+ endpoints covering influencer, affiliate, commission, UGC and loyalty. Production ready.

Wallets and settlement

Provider wallet with 20+ transaction types and reserve-hold, guide wallet with cash and points, and a commission ledger running Pending to Approved to Paid.

Attribution

Affiliate links with UTM tracking and fraud detection; eight attribution event types with geographic and device data.

Queue and job infrastructure

RabbitMQ with seven queues, dead-letter handling and auto-recovery; a job system with retries and SHA256 idempotency; n8n already dispatching.

The mechanism

Automation with a hand on it.

Three execution modes, and a rule engine that learns which interventions actually worked.

Hybrid is the default

AI drafts, humans approve, influencers execute, ads run partly automated. Full auto and fully human-managed both exist for the ends of the risk range.

Risk-based approval

An automation policy sets the budget above which a human must approve. Small decisions run themselves; expensive ones do not.

Five layers, one loop

Events, metrics, rule evaluation, action execution, then learning — action history stores before-and-after metrics so the engine can tell which rules earn their place.

Reputation that compounds

Two scores per squad member: project performance and a global reputation across every provider. Elite tier earns a 15% commission multiplier and priority matching — a reason for good operators to stay on the platform.

The model

Simple model. Compounding revenue.

Subscription is the floor; commission grows with the provider; licensing is the layer that arrives once the network has value of its own.

Provider subscription

Starter EGP 299, Growth EGP 599, Pro EGP 999 a month, plus featured placement at EGP 500–2,000. Blended ARPU EGP 550.

Commission per booking

8–12% of the booking. An average event is EGP 3,500 and an average beauty booking EGP 450, so platform take runs EGP 36–420 per booking.

Revenue per provider

EGP 800–4,200 a month once subscription and commission are combined — the reason ARPU rises without a new sale.

Platform licensing

EGP 50K setup and EGP 8K a month for API access per consumer frontend. Payback in 12–18 months at 90%+ gross margin.

Honest state

Where it actually is.

Stated plainly, because an investor will check.

LIVE

Web platform

Full provider dashboard — onboarding, services, calendar, CRM, payments and analytics, running at shaaml.online in Arabic and English.

LIVE

API-first distribution

.NET Core backend with documented APIs. OurBride is already a consumer frontend consuming provider data, availability and booking flows.

LIVE

Payments and settlement

Payment rails integrated, providers settled, transaction commission collected automatically.

BUILT, NOT PUBLISHED

Mobile app

The Flutter app is built and signed — the Apple provisioning profile for com.shaaml.app runs to February 2027. It is not on the App Store or Google Play today. Publishing it is days of work, and it is the fastest credibility win available.

Revenue at scale

Providers are onboarded and bookings are processed. What is unproven is a provider paying month after month at the ARPU the model assumes.
